origin: Original workshop built by Muse (AI assistant) on 19 November 2026 at Steven Powell's direction, from his own design notes in the Everyday Cool ideas side chat that evening. Of the four queued STEM rooms he ordered saved that night (Math, Engineering, Earth, Computing — 'save that list I want to do them all'), Engineering went first; Math is second, on his word: 'Then we can do math.' His notes, built to here: a tricks bench led by the nines table written as two columns ('the 09 in one column and 9 - 0 in the other'), every trick carrying its why, with number theory in plain language; simple algebra and the common formulas, each with a worked example; huge and tiny numbers in scientific notation with Avogadro's number as the bridge exhibit into Everyday Chemistry; a simple JavaScript scientific calculator whose honesty line is floating point's last-digit lie (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004, computed live by the visitor's own machine on the page); one button producing a printable spreadsheet-style sheet with the times table to 16x16 and a log table reaching 1000 by characteristic + mantissa, with proportional-parts interpolation notes; and his standing order that the STEM rooms carry Wikipedia and other links on their pages (thirteen destinations, verified live). The room carries the FULL log table (901 mantissas, 1.00-9.99) where Everyday Engineering carries the pocket one (91), and the two rooms' log sections link to each other both ways — closing, in this build, the cross-link Engineering's COLLECTION.md recorded as pending when that room shipped hours earlier. It enters the catalog under 'Science' with hubParent 'stem-room', immediately after Everyday Engineering, as the twenty-seventh entry and the STEM Room's eighth workshop. This folder is the maintained original. Web-first, per Steven's plan set the same evening: the four queue rooms go live on the web one at a time and reach the desktop app together in a single later release.
